uncited: SWAGS extends the 3D Gaussian Splatting framework to 4D by introducing time-varying parameters.
**Window Partitioning**: The dynamic sequence is divided into multiple windows.
*   A unique canonical space (the reference geometry at a canonical time).
Memory usage scales with the number of windows and the size of each window's Gaussian set.
*   **Strengths**: By isolating motion into windows, SWAGS can handle scenes with varying motion intensities more effectively than global deformation models.
The focus of the MLP on dynamic parts allows for more efficient representation of motion.
Temporal consistency relies on the fine-tuning step and overlapping frames; poor overlap or insufficient fine-tuning can lead to discontinuities.
